proposed_lead: Ol Chiki gives Santali readers a writing system with letters and marks for its sounds. Follow the script into learning resources, poems and literary conversations.

paragraphs.text: Santali was already being spoken and written when Raghunath Murmu developed Ol Chiki. The President’s Secretariat’s account of the February 2026 celebration credits him with creating it in 1925, and names Roman, Devanagari, Odia and Bengali among the scripts previously used for Santali. The date belongs to the history of a writing system; it is not the beginning of the language.

That distinction changes how you approach a page. Santali names the language; Ol Chiki names one way of writing it. A reader’s spoken language alone does not tell you which script they learned, or which editions they can comfortably read. Begin with both questions.

sections.title: Vowels have letters of their own

paragraphs.text: Ol Chiki runs from left to right. Its vowels are written as separate letters, rather than being carried as an inherent vowel within a consonant. The Unicode Standard describes additional marks that distinguish sounds: a raised dot marks nasalization, while a separate length mark can follow a vowel. The shapes on the page do more than identify the script; their arrangement gives the reader information about sound.

Look at a short printed line with a willing reader or teacher. Ask them to point out a vowel letter and explain a mark that changes how it is read. Following one example carefully is a better beginning than treating a row of unfamiliar letters as decoration.

A November 2018 booklet published by the Special Development Council, Mayurbhanj, places English, Odia and Santali alongside one another. Its compilers are Mangat Murmu, Raghunath Hembram and Saluram Hembram. It offers a specific resource to begin with, and named people whose work should remain attached to it.

The column headings name languages; check the script as well when choosing a learning resource. Pick one entry with a fluent reader and ask how they would use it in a sentence. Keep their explanation separate from the printed wording, especially if their local usage differs.

For a literary reading lead, seek Nalha by Gobinda Chandra Majhi, listed as poetry in Sahitya Akademi’s 2016 Santali award entry. The award supplies an author and a title, not a reading of the poems. Ask for an edition and record its script and any translator before beginning.

At a Baripada symposium on 21 May 2022, discussion extended from writing to the organised work of keeping a language in public life. Sahitya Akademi’s annual report records Damayanti Beshra chairing the inaugural session and speaking about Santali’s status. Later papers examined language, script and literary movements in Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal. This gives Mayurbhanj’s literary setting a concrete connection to a wider conversation.
